system.description: Easy (1d) Magical Sight checks include determining the colour of a magical aura, identifying auras that incorporate more than one colour, distinguishing between different auras in locations where there are multiple auras close together, identifying the strength of a magical effect or aura, or identifying a spell cast that your character already knows. Difficult (2{Dc}) tasks include determining the purpose or nature of an enchantment or magic item, locating a particular magical aura in an area crowded with magic (such as picking out the only Chaos sorcerer in a room crowded with coll sﬁe wizards), identifying a spell being cast that the character does not personally know, or gauging how much power a spellcaster is currently maintaining. Daunting (4{Dc}) tasks include detecting the presence of magic through a physical Sight obstruction such as a wall or door, tracing a spell or effect back to its source after it has been cast, or detecting the remnants of an aura that is no longer present. Expend a manoeuvre and a skill check - generally, anything that would impair an Observation skill check has a similar impact on Magical Sight checks. The exception to this is darkness. Since auras are visible as a glow of light, magical sight is actually more effective in darkness and less effective in especially bright daylight. Average (2{Dc}) tasks include determining the colour of a magical aura within one room or locating the only magical aura in a room. In all cases, a weaker aura is more difficult to detect than a stronger one. For example, while all wizards possess a magical aura, the aura of an apprentice wizard might only be detectable if one is close enough to be considered engaged. A Wizard Lord, however, may be surrounded by a nimbus of light from his Wind of Magic, detectable from a distance of several streets. Obstructions that block vision also obstruct magical sight. For example, a magical aura would be more difficult to discern in the fog, just as an object is visually obscured by the fog. In all cases, a weaker aura is more difficult to detect than a stronger one.
